View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/a8b47942-89da-4f9e-a0d6-c4eb6a08dda1/In_partnership_with...__2_.png?t=1738624639)
Follow image link: (https://fnf.dev/3EeVtXj)
Caption: 

Welcome, humans. 

It looks like OpenAI’s money-hungry days might be behind it—SoftBank is [willing to spend](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/02/03/softbank-commits-to-joint-venture-with-openai.html) $3B per year on OpenAI products for itself and all its subsidiaries through a joint venture called SB OpenAI Japan. 

The deal basically created a new tier of ChatGPT that SoftBank CEO Masayoshi Son called “Cristal Intelligence.” You get Operator, you get Deep Research, ChatGPT Enterprise, access to the API, and even custom models. 

Interested? Just convince your CFO to drop $3B on a bunch of stuff you can basically get in ChatGPT Pro. _Good luck! _

**Here’s what you need to know about AI today:**

* We tested Deep Research and share the results. 

* Meta outlined what AI systems it won’t open-source. 

* An AI-enhanced Beatles recording won Grammy. 

* Code tweak could cut data center energy by 30%. 

Advertise in The Neuron here. (https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfng1Qz3wGLc_-f9goa1TQgnGE_rehbW55Gx5VaEYIhn4OueQ/viewform)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8725d956-e5e7-4b68-90a6-08a1aaebeacf/Neuron-Page-Splitters3.png)
Caption: 

# Who researched it better…ChatGPT or Gemini? 

On Sunday, OpenAI launched [Deep Research](https://openai.com/index/introducing-deep-research/) (DR for short), but we barely had enough time to [cover the announcement](https://www.theneurondaily.com/p/the-new-chatgpt-o3-mini), let alone try it out. So today, we’re putting GPT Deep Research to the test in a head to head battle against [Gemini Deep Research](https://blog.google/products/gemini/google-gemini-deep-research/) across 3 key prompts—and you can vote for the winner. 

These prompts were hand-picked by you—and whenever possible, we ran them exactly as you submitted them. 

_In our best WWE voice: “Arrrre yoooou ready to reseaaarrrch ruuuumbbbble??!”_

**First prompt—”the product review”: **“Research the best car I could buy for 20k.”

1. [**GPT DR’s result**](https://chatgpt.com/share/67a15d8e-0eb8-8003-b222-5a4729d3665c): _Very_ thorough. It covered most aspects of what we suggested, but it was too long to read, so we asked it “which is the best” at the end.  

2. [**Gemini DR’s result**](https://g.co/gemini/share/9dafe2096ff7): Apparently Gemini researched 481 websites—the most we’ve _EVER _seen Gemini comb through—to get this answer. 

Oh, and here’s a [lifetime ownership cost analysis](https://chatgpt.com/share/67a1637f-4a14-8003-8f77-adbd8444f323) between a Tesla Model 3, Toyota Prius, and a Camry—_in case you were curious. _

**Next prompt—”the how to guide”: **“Best ways to start and write cold emails in times of mailbox spams and repetitive, boring intros.” 

1. [**GPT DR’s take**](https://chatgpt.com/share/67a16409-1d80-8003-9327-28dfebf76100): at first, it seemed like it was working—until we realized it was totally gaslighting us. After a bit of prompting, we got it to ACTUALLY work; but when we [prompted it a second time](https://chatgpt.com/share/67a1688c-68e4-8003-a194-68ad433d2d44), it went much better.  

2. [**Gemini DR**](https://gemini.google.com/share/2718f022e82f): this was pretty thorough, decent advice; although I will say the templates were pretty generic, and that doesn’t really address the pain point. 

Btw, you could totally upload these answers into GPT and ask it to create custom templates for your specific needs—just saying! 

**Prompt #3—“the rabbit hole”: **“Research multiverse theories and draw a conclusion about whether the current state of research and theory suggests it may be true or not.”

1. **[GPT DR’s answer](https://chatgpt.com/share/67a16236-9570-8003-9538-44862b59bd1f)****:** _Mind blown—_that’s all we’ll say. Well, that and it sounds like GPT DR is leaning towards “multiverse = true.” 

2. [**Gemini DR**](https://g.co/gemini/share/fb1e9b89de10): A bit less depth, but still interesting—seems like Gemini leans towards “not true.” Fascinating!

**Now, there were a few other searches we tried that weren’t so clear cut**…and some Gemini just wouldn’t answer. Here’s a quick round-up of a few of those: 

1. “What are the main strategies for reducing recidivism in the UK” ([GPT’s answer](https://chatgpt.com/share/67a16511-2210-8003-8a70-bc37351438c1), [Gemini’s answer](https://g.co/gemini/share/1866c3a942cc)). 

2. “How will Trump’s Presidency + DeepSeek impact AI advances” ([GPT’s answer](https://chatgpt.com/share/67a1615d-3938-8003-9856-b271b60fff83); Gemini wouldn’t touch this one). 

3. “Explain a technical paper and do a sample implementation with sample data” ([GPT’s answer](https://chatgpt.com/share/67a1668a-a4c4-8003-97cc-4da16ba03ffa)—if you’re an AI researcher reading this, let us know if it worked! Here’s [Gemini’s answer](https://gemini.google.com/share/dba56cf27803)…) 

**BONUS: **Here’s a few GPT DR results we found from around the web: 

* Act like a [financial analyst](https://chatgpt.com/share/67a10a0c-e198-8004-9803-55cf77b8cf59) and write an in-depth report on NVIDIA. _Not financial advice _😉_ _

* Generate a report on how to use AI as a [freelance consultant](https://chatgpt.com/share/67a0c391-19f4-800d-8618-e03525fe799a).

* Under what condition can you get a [visa to work in Spain](https://chatgpt.com/share/67a0d75b-9bd4-800d-9f9e-9fb264d910d6)?

GPT DR seems to _really_ work. It produces a ton of content in its reports; the question now is: does it actually write TOO much?

###### **FROM OUR PARTNERS**

# Zep / AI That Thinks Beyond Static Data

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9874c8cb-ea58-4819-8338-2291023d1e90/Screenshot_2025-02-03_at_3.06.24_PM_1.png?t=1738632471)
Follow image link: (https://fnf.dev/3EeVtXj)
Caption: 

[Zep](https://fnf.dev/3EeVtXj) is transforming how AI agents remember and learn. Traditional systems retrieve static documents, but [Zep](https://fnf.dev/3EeVtXj)’s temporal knowledge graph continuously evolves, tracking conversations and structured business data over time. This means more accurate responses, faster performance, and a deeper understanding of context. 

With 94.8% DMR accuracy—surpassing MemGPT—[Zep](https://fnf.dev/3EeVtXj) not only remembers across sessions but reasons over time. It also reduces token costs, making it scalable and enterprise-ready.

Say goodbye to fragmented AI memory—Zep delivers real intelligence that adapts as your data changes. [Learn more](https://fnf.dev/3EeVtXj) 

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/81bc93b8-d709-4561-83bb-7c42b9d9ad1a/Neuron-Page-Splitters4.png)
Caption: 

# Prompt Tip of the Day

Since o3-mini is available to free users, it’s an incredibly powerful tool that everybody can take advantage of (unlike Deep Research, Operator, and other tools limited at the Pro level). 

Here’s a prompt template we came up with [using o3-mini to search](https://chatgpt.com/share/67a075ed-073c-8003-88a2-a4f185298e31) for prompt advice on o3-mini. 

And here’s what happened when we used Deep Research to [ask the same thing](https://chatgpt.com/share/67a1727d-b55c-8003-8406-82c968c792c1).  

We’re not entirely sure these will work for your needs, but try them out, and let us know what you think of the end result with the poll below.  

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8cb2b4bd-f1cf-4f08-a638-d713c9774aa2/image.png?t=1734252666)
Caption: 

# Treats To Try.

1. [Anthropic](https://www.ft.com/content/cf11ebd8-aa0b-4ed4-945b-a5d4401d186e) has a new system called a “[constitutional classifier](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.18837)” that adds a constitution of rules over a language model to stop jailbreaks—[try it out here](https://claude.ai/constitutional-classifiers).

2. [Tana](https://tana.inc/?utm_source=theneuron) transforms your meetings and notes into organized, searchable tasks and projects that update automatically as you work ([raised $25M](https://techcrunch.com/2025/02/03/tana-snaps-up-25m-with-its-ai-powered-knowledge-graph-for-work-racking-up-a-160k-waitlist/)).

3. [Sonofa](https://sonofa.ai/?utm_source=theneuron) turns your reading materials into podcasts you can listen to anywhere.

4. [Skyvern](https://www.skyvern.com/?utm_source=theneuron) handles your tedious web tasks by automatically filling forms, downloading documents, and checking out purchases across any website.

5. [Chat Thing](https://chatthing.ai/) turns your business content into 24/7 customer support bots that work across your website, Slack, and Discord.

6. [Presentation 2.0](https://getcube.one/?utm_source=theneuron) turns any conversation into a ready-to-share presentation, complete with slides and narration.

[See our top 51 AI Tools for Business here!](https://www.theneuron.ai/top-tools)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/d59f9bfb-e597-47fa-80c4-0151d4495aa9/Neuron-Page-Splitters5.png)
Caption: 

# Around the Horn.

* [Meta](https://techcrunch.com/2025/02/03/meta-says-it-may-stop-development-of-ai-systems-it-deems-too-risky/)’s new [policy document](https://ai.meta.com/static-resource/meta-frontier-ai-framework/?utm_source=newsroom&utm_medium=web&utm_content=Frontier_AI_Framework_PDF&utm_campaign=Our_Approach_to_Frontier_AI_blog) (known as the Frontier AI Framework) outlines what types of AI it won’t open-source: “high risk” systems that make cyber-crimes and biological attacks easier to carry out, and “critical risk” systems that basically guarantee a catastrophic outcome. 

* [The Beatles](https://techcrunch.com/2025/02/03/the-beatles-won-a-grammy-last-night-thanks-to-ai/) won a grammy thanks to a noise-reduction AI that helped Paul McCartney clean up an old piano demo. 

* Researchers in Canada [showed](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/data-centres-energy-reduction-code/) that data centers can reduce their energy usage by 30% just from altering ~30 lines of code. 

* Speaking of head to head showdowns—check out this [match-up](https://www.tomsguide.com/ai/i-tested-deepseek-vs-qwen-2-5-with-7-prompts-heres-the-winner?utm_source=flipboard&utm_content=topic/computerscience) comparing [DeepSeek R1](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1) and [Qwen 2.5](https://qwenlm.github.io/blog/qwen2.5-max/) across 7 prompts. 

* **Fun fact: **if you want to ignore a good chunk of AI generated results in your regular internet searches, [try swearing](https://www.pcworld.com/article/2596403/want-better-google-search-results-start-swearing.html)—it’s not a silver bullet for better content, but it’ll help avoid a good chunk of AI slop!

* **B.S:** “Tariff assessment and free trade agreements.”

* **J.N: **“Identify the operator of a website that has no contact information published on it. Then, do lead research on that company.”

* **C.S: **“To summarize my work every week from my transcripts from my meeting transcript AI system. It does not have a way to download them so I need it to click the ... and download each one and then I want a summary for each day by topics and then one for the week that I can send to my boss :P”
